text:
maria (partnerships): Heads-up: EdgeSilicon wants to ship OpenArbor-7B in two ways: (A) embedded quantized weights inside their SI appliance, (B) a managed/hosted listing in their cloud marketplace. Need legal + infra alignment on redistribution rules and announcement timing.
jamal (bd): They confirmed both. SI team needs a downloadable 4-bit package for offline installs; marketplace ops want an on-demand hosted SKU.
sara-legal: Before we commit to downloads we need to parse OpenArbor's license and their v1.2 redistribution addendum. Key asks likely: provenance metadata, attribution, no rebranding, and restrictions on downstream resale. I'll review.
kevin-eng: Tech note: shipping quantized artifacts means we must produce reproducible quant runs and include conversion tooling. EdgeSilicon uses a custom kernel that expects a specific layout; we'll need a compatibility shim and tests.
tasha-ops: For downloads, ops requires signed artifacts (GPG or Sigstore), a manifest with checksums, and a partner entitlement flow in the marketplace. We can implement conditional geoblock per partner.
liz-marketing: Co-launch window request: EdgeSilicon wants simultaneous marketplace listing + PR. Marketing needs 21 business days for collateral, logo approvals, legal clearance of copy, and embargo coordination.
sara-legal: My proposed commercial redistribution paths: (1) Hosted Offering: Redwood hosts model, revenue share with EdgeSilicon for marketplace referrals; (2) Certified SI Distribution: we provide signed quantized weights to named customers under a redistribution addendum (metadata + limited license, no broad resale). Addendum to include security patch cadence and attribution.
jamal (bd): Commercial ask: EdgeSilicon prefers higher split for hosted given they operate marketplace traffic. For SI downloads they'll accept a per-deployment license fee plus co-marketing credits.
kevin-eng: Checklist for delivery: ``- reproducible quant artifact (.tar.gz + sha256 + signature) - conversion scripts and model_card.md - unit/CI that re-creates quant and validates outputs - compatibility shim repo with integration tests``
maria (partnerships): Sara: export control risk? EdgeSilicon serves APAC and ME/SEA.
sara-legal: OpenArbor maintainers flagged potential dual-use for specialized tokenizers. I'll run an export classification. Until cleared, recommend APAC downloads be gated. Hosted region-restrict is simpler to start with.
tasha-ops: Ops can implement geo-restrictions on downloads and SKU entitlements. For hosted we can offer two SKUs: "EdgeSilicon Managed (global)" and "EdgeSilicon Managed (restricted)". We will also require partner SSO for download access.
liz-marketing: Timeline: T-21 collateral, T-10 legal signoff, T-3 embargo approval. If geo restrictions apply we'll adapt PR text.
jamal (bd): Action on commercial terms: I'll send initial term sheet (rev share + per-download fee) and get EdgeSilicon's counters.
sara-legal: I'll draft a redistribution addendum template: provenance header format, attribution language, no-derivative rebranding clause, 12-month limited redistribution without renewal, and a security patch SLA.
kevin-eng: Also recommend we ship a small integration test harness for the SI appliance that exercises warm-start, KV cache, and a sample prompts set to avoid runtime surprises.
maria (partnerships): Action items: - sara-legal: license review + draft addendum + export classification (due Thu EOD) - kevin-eng: quant pipeline docs + reproducibility CI (PR by next Tue) - tasha-ops: entitlement + signed artifact flow + geoblock runbook (due next Wed) - liz-marketing: draft timeline + asset list (first draft in 3 days) - jamal: commercial term sheet to EdgeSilicon (sync Fri)
deploy-bot: Reminder: create repo stub under org/redwood-partners/edge-silicon with README, integration checklist, and artifact spec.
maria (partnerships): EdgeSilicon also asked for privacy-preserving performance telemetry (opt-in) to monitor model latency/quality. Any red flags?
sara-legal: Telemetry must be opt-in, aggregated, and PII-free. We'll need a DPA addendum and DSAR paths documented.
kevin-eng: Feasible: emit hashed prompt shapes, token counts, and binned latency histograms. No raw prompts. Make opt-in toggled at runtime and documented in the addendum.
jamal (bd): EdgeSilicon liked that. They want a short customer-facing blurb: "privacy-first, opt-in telemetry; aggregated signals only."
maria (partnerships): Sounds good. If legal + ops are aligned, marketing can start the creative tomorrow. Reconvene Friday after jamal's commercial sync. :rocket:
